chunks.l2:
[tal-a12-v01] Now the use of this path, our present subject, is set forth.

[tal-a12-v10] Unshaking contemplation of fullness brings firmness; and through inner-mutter practice, reflecting, one becomes a mantra-vessel.

[tal-a12-v02] Thus this whole path, as it rests in consciousness, through that rests also in void, intellect, breath, channel-wheels, and bodies.

[tal-a12-v03] And outside too, everywhere in liṅga, image, fire, altar and the rest; so it stands, whole and part-wise, in sequence and all at once.

[tal-a12-v04] Laid out from consciousness-principle to the outer, this path: at each level one should make one's own form shine, by own freedom, in fitting form.

[tal-a12-v05] And everything's form everywhere — even his does not not shine; for we cannot bear exclusion anywhere, even in dream.

[tal-a12-v06] Thus one should behold the body as filled with the universe-path, painted by time's activity — the abode of pulsation made of space and time.

[tal-a12-v07] So beheld, he is made of the deities within the universe; to be meditated, worshipped, libated — entered then, one is freed.

[tal-a12-v08] Thus pot, cloth, liṅga, altar, book, water — or whatever one may see anywhere: there one should reach identity-with-that.

[tal-a12-v09] Therein offering of things is held worship through non-difference; and contemplation of full-formedness is called meditation.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a12-v11] Effecting the melting of self-difference of the beings offered therein, their ray-rich being he should bestow — devoted to the fire-rite.

[tal-a12-v12] For one so acting, seeing all with equal eye, unwaveringness is the pure vow — evenness taught in the Nandiśikhā.

[tal-a12-v13] Thus through worship, japa, meditation, fire-offering, vow, and rule in sequence, the ancients called the complete state absorption.

[tal-a12-v14] Here in worship, japa and the rest, whether outward or inward, there is no rule at all about materials, nor any prohibition.

[tal-a12-v15] No use here whatsoever for visualization, purification, twilight-rites and the rest; and in the Trika Sūtra it is said sacrifice arises toward the rite.

[tal-a12-v16] Not knowing rule, knowing rule, and 'thus' and so on at length: when, as, by which, where one's own consciousness is gracious.

[tal-a12-v17] Then, so, by that, there: each respective enjoyable — and that is the rule; all, worldly and unworldly, one should employ here by that.

[tal-a12-v18] In steadiness: but the trembler should forcibly diminish tremor — by force, as, by whatever means, in sequence or all at once, or.

[tal-a12-v19] Doubt melts within — so he should become striving; the goddesses resting in mind, rite, and senses he should libate with forbidden things indeed.

[tal-a12-v20] And the hero-vow one should salute — thus the Bhargaśikhā word: for doubt is impurity, weariness, contraction — thus this.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a12-v21] Inside the world-prison it forges gross-post shackles; mantras are letter-natured, substance five-elemented.

[tal-a12-v22] The breathing kind which is consciousness-selfed — where is mixture there, how? With mixture absent, what is this doubt — even hers clearly baseless.

[tal-a12-v23] One should not doubt; thus doubt dissolves through disregard — in the Sarvācāra, Vīrālī, Niśācara, Krama and the rest.

[tal-a12-v24] And this is spread in the śāstras — there it is said: for from doubt arises weariness, from doubt being a vessel of obstacles.

[tal-a12-v25] And said Utpaladeva, the venerable guru of my guru: the all-doubt thunderbolt path — we bow to the Māheśvara path.

[tal-a12-v26] For attaining the anuttara state, this āṇava with means shown at great length — indeed, make it grow, O wise ones!
